keyTerms.definition: Adds -inf above the diagonal before softmax; future weights exactly zero.
x + f(norm(x)); the highway stays exact.
norm(x + f(x)); the norm sits on the gradient path.
Rotates Q/K pairs by position-dependent angles; the dot product depends on relative distance.

recall.question: Why is attention scaled by 1/sqrt(dh)?
recall.answer: QK^T has variance dh under unit-variance components; without the scale softmax saturates and gradients vanish.

recall.question: What breaks if residual connections are removed?
recall.answer: Gradients lose the identity path; deep stacks stop training past a few layers.

keyTerms.definition: Softmax over one query's scores; L1.2's hand computation.
Sweep the scale, expect peak gradient health near 1/sqrt(dh).

recall.question: What are the invariants of stable masked attention?
recall.answer: Rows sum to 1, future weights zero.

recall.question: What indicts the missing scale in L1.5's debug?

keyTerms.definition: x/rms x g, no mean subtraction, unlike LayerNorm.
dy/dx = I + J_f; the identity term survives even when J_f vanishes.

recall.question: State the zero-block test for each wiring.
recall.answer: Pre-norm: zero blocks give output == input. Post-norm: zero blocks give output == norm(input).

keyTerms.definition: FFN dominates scores 6.0x alone, 3.0x counting scores+mix.
68.7 GFLOP scores vs 412.3 GFLOP FFN: 6.0x alone.

recall.question: Which dominates in E1's block, and by what factor?
recall.answer: FFN dominates: 6.0x on scores alone, 3.0x counting scores+mix.

keyTerms.definition: Highest frequency i=0 gives w = 1; angle at position 100 is 100 radians.
Leaves w_0 = 1 unchanged; stretches the low-frequency pairs.

recall.question: What happens to the highest-frequency angle if the RoPE base doubles?
recall.answer: Nothing: w_0 = 1 is unchanged, so the angle does not move; the base stretches the low-frequency pairs.

keyTerms.definition: cos/sin lack the head axis, so (1,1,T,dh//2) misaligns against (B,T,h,dh//2).
cos/sin lack it: (1,1,T,dh//2) misaligns against (B,T,h,dh//2).

recall.question: What is the RoPE bug and the fix?
recall.answer: cos/sin have shape (1,1,T,dh//2) but xr[...,0] has (B,T,h,dh//2); the head axis is absent. Fix: index as np.cos(ang)[None, :, None, :].

recall.question: What invariants does the fix restore?
recall.answer: Norm preservation and shift invariance of dot products.

keyTerms.definition: Exact attention without materializing (B,h,T,T) weights; the memory replacement.
The (B,h,T,T) weights and cache: memory breakage at T=131072.

recall.question: At T=131072, what breaks and what replaces it?
recall.answer: FLOPs: the T^2 attention scores; replacement: a subquadratic attention variant (U04) or sequence parallelism (U09). Memory: the (B,h,T,T) weights and KV cache; replacement: tiled exact attention (U07) plus KV quantization or sharing (U04).

keyTerms.definition: Sharing QKV or FFN weights across layers; saves L-1 copies.
Option 1: shrink dff by the needed ratio; params scale linearly.

recall.question: Name the two 30-percent param-cut options and their costs.
recall.answer: Option 1: shrink dff; SwiGLU params 3xd xdff scale linearly. Option 2: tie QKV or FFN weights across layers, saving L-1 copies. Cost: capacity loss; sharing also couples gradients across layers.

keyTerms.definition: Running past training length; the first gap.
Testing the claimed property numerically, e.g. shift-invariance.

recall.question: Name the three gaps in the position-encoding paper and their closes.
recall.answer: (1) No length extrapolation test: run past training length. (2) No RoPE baseline: ablate head-to-head at matched compute. (3) No mechanism analysis: test the claimed property numerically.
